International Applicants
Brandeis has a rich history of welcoming students from around the world, with students joining us from over 100 countries. International students are an integral part of our community, bringing varied perspectives that enrich our classrooms and campus.
Graduate English Language Proficiency Requirements Effective Fall 2026
For international students applying for graduate study, English Language Proficiency can be shown by either
meeting one or more of the below English Language Test waiver options
or
submitting a current (not-expired) TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English language test as part of their applications.
English Language Test Waiver Eligibility
Students who meet one or more of the below criteria can submit their application without an English Language test score:
Completed an on-campus bachelor’s degree with at least three full-time academic years of study where English was the ONLY language of instruction. (Please note: English as the language of instruction should be indicated on the institution’s website, transcript and/or mark sheets.)
Completed at least one full-time academic year of on-campus graduate study (master’s level degree or higher) where English was the ONLY language of instruction. (Please note: English as the language of instruction should be indicated on the institution’s website, transcript and/or mark sheets.)
Worked full-time for two years in the United States within the last four years. To be considered “full-time” work in this instance, students must have completed this work after their bachelor’s degree and work at least 35 hours per week.
If one or more of the above conditions is met, no additional English Language Proficiency requirements are needed at time of application submission. However, Brandeis may request supplemental materials if deemed necessary as part of the application review process.
The Brandeis University TOEFL code is 3122.
English Language Test Requirements
Applicants who do not meet the above waiver criteria must submit TOEFL (including the iBT Home Edition), IELTS (IELTS Indicator and IELTS Online) or Duolingo English Test scores. Our Admissions Committee takes a holistic approach to reviewing applications and considers each part of a student's application to evaluate communication abilities and fit for the program. If an applicant believes their English Language Skills are in line with the academic rigor of graduate study, we encourage them to apply.
TOEFL: We recommend a TOEFL iBT score of at least 5.0 (please note: this is equivalent to a score of 100 on the TOEFL iBT exam taken prior to January 21, 2026) or a TOEFL ITP score of at least 627.
IELTS score of at least 7.0.
Duolingo English Test score of at least 130 or PTE Academic score of at least 68.
Unofficial or official test scores can be submitted as part of the online application. However, official test scores are required only if you accept an offer of admission.
Official TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo English Test and PTE scores are valid for up to two years. Test scores must be valid at the time the application is submitted. If your test score will expire prior to the start of the program, you must submit your official test score prior to its expiration date.

International Students and Scholars Office
The International Students and Scholars Office (ISSO) supports Brandeis international students and scholars throughout their time spent in the Brandeis community. ISSO issues visa documents, assists with immigration procedures, facilitates educational programming, and provides advising on academic, financial and personal matters.
